reviews.title: WAS A must in this stage of my life.
reviews.body:
New review: I loved this app until it accidentally updated. I always intentionally avoid updates for various reasons, then wait until they work out inevitable bugs, but for all the newer features that are nice…there are a slew of issues that make this near useless for me. For instance… I built many playlists that I listen to often. I could stay in practice seamlessly, study for hours, fall asleep, whatever I chose. The screen would dim but the tracks would continue to play. Now, if the screen dims, or if I try to go dark to try and fall asleep, it illuminates after each track and stops so I have to hit play after every single track…what’s the point of wasting hours of time building playlists that don’t work and function like playlists???

The preview option is redundant and irritating and I see no way to turn it off. If I tapped a track before, it played 20-30 seconds of the track. That way I could tell if I liked the subject, voice, music, background, recording quality, etc. Now it goes to a different screen with a bunch of other tracks that have nothing in common with the one I want to just hear for a few seconds, and if I’m building a playlist it takes twice as long if I’m focusing on one teacher because I have to exit out of 2screens not just one and now it’s been over an hour of me trying to just meditate when I would’ve completed my nightly routine and been at calm, but it’s essentially useless. 

Who wants to snap out of meditation every 10-15, or even 30 minutes to hit play because now there are quadruple redundant steps to do what the old school system did flawlessly. I’m about to cancel my subscription, or..it could just be that instead of this being an easy lovely peaceful app like it has been the last few years for me, it’s turned into a nightmare.

reviews.title: Lost its mission
reviews.body:
I’ve used Insight Timer for many years and have always appreciated what the app stood for: making meditation accessible to as many people as possible.

Unfortunately, over the last few years, it feels like the focus has shifted more toward monetization than accessibility. Features that were previously available with the free membership have gradually been removed or placed behind the paid subscription. I completely understand charging for premium content and features, but even some very basic sounds and options now require an upgrade.

What’s especially frustrating is the constant pop-ups encouraging you to upgrade while trying to use the free version. It makes the experience feel less peaceful and more like a sales funnel, which seems contrary to the purpose of a meditation app.

I don’t mind paying for a valuable service, but I wish Insight Timer would maintain a genuinely useful free experience while offering additional premium features for those who choose to upgrade. After being a longtime user, it’s disappointing to see the direction the app has taken.

reviews.title: There needs to me some tweaks
reviews.body:
This is a great app, and I’ve learned a lot from it. There’s a massive amount of content available, which I really appreciate. That said, there are a few things that I think would make the app significantly better:

1)Too many steps to get to the content I want. There are too many checkpoints and prompts when opening the app. I don’t think there needs to be a quote and questions every time I open it. I use Insight Timer specifically for anxiety and stress, and when I need the app, I’m often looking for something that will help me right away. Having to navigate through several screens before getting to the content I want can actually add more stress and anxiety.

2)There should be a “Skip Intro” button. I appreciate that many courses and meditations include longer introductions for people who are listening for the first time. However, if I’ve already heard the introduction, I should be able to skip it and get straight to the content.

3)Challenges and courses aren’t saving my progress/location. For some reason, the challenges and courses I’m currently working through aren’t staying easily accessible. Every day, I have to navigate through the app to find the challenge or course I’m working on. It would be much better if these were saved prominently so I could quickly pick up where I left off.

Overall, the content on Insight Timer is excellent, and I really value having so much of it available. The interface is good, but with these relatively simple tweaks, I think it could be WAY better and much easier to use especially for people who are turning to the app when they’re already stressed or anxious.

reviews.title: Forcing video into my mindfulness practice? Absolutely not.
reviews.body:
As someone who works in media, I’m keenly aware of how insidious the “pivot to video” creep has become. My favorite meditation app was the last place I expected it to show up. 

I’ve been a dedicated Insight Timer user for over a decade. It’s where I go to unplug, ground myself and literally *close my eyes.* What’s kept me loyal to IT is how calming and low-stimulation the user experience is — it used to be so simple and practical, like the Reddit of meditation apps. I loved that it never really changed. So waking up one morning to find a carousel of *meditation videos* (who is asking for these, seriously?) suddenly featured at the top of the home screen, with no way to turn the feature off, feels manipulative and totally inconsistent with the app’s original purpose. Seeing so many faces staring back at me (with sleek, professional lighting and backgrounds) when I’ve opened the app specifically to get away from that vibe grosses me out, like self-improvement is being TikTokified.

Miss me with this redesign. If there truly is a demand for video content in this space (which I find hard to fathom), there are ways to meet it without forcing the rest of us to go down the scroll hole with you. I’m taking my meditation practice elsewhere, and I hope everyone serious about their practice does too.

reviews.title: It’s annoying
reviews.body: It is a good app and very helpful. It really helps my anxiety but the biggest problem is that whenever I use (usually when needing urgent relaxation), I have to click through 15 screens asking me how I’m feeling, how often I’m going to be using it, whether I want to buy content. Big turn off
it is reduntant

reviews.title: Liars
reviews.body: Was told I would be reminded when my 7 day trial was over and I was not. I didn’t like the app and was charged $60 anyways when I deleted it. Do not trust this developer, they want to take money from poor single moms

reviews.title: Playlists broken
reviews.body:
Playlists have been broken for me for weeks. I can no longer listen to my curated sleep playlists. Every time it stops after the first track. Support tried to help, but nothing has been resolved. I’ve uninstalled, created new playlists, etc. but nothing works. I now have to be content with one track unless I want to open the app each time and select the next. 

The constant UI changes are also frustrating. Having to constantly figure out where I am and where my favorites are is annoying. Also the amount of steps you have to go through after a track takes me out of any calm mindset I achieve. Asking for ratings, the slow running day count screen, this and that. Not everything needs to be so convoluted. I guess I need to go find a meditation for anger now.

reviews.title: Just be a timer
reviews.body: This app has grown more and more complicated to the point that I seem to be required to complete a questionnaire every time I want to access the timer. Booo on overcomplicated ‘wellness’

reviews.title: Down hill
reviews.body: I used to really like this app with a paid member for several years and at that time it was a great app. But in the last few years, it’s gotten more and more like a game and more and more like I’m there to answer their marketing questions. I opened the app today to meditate and there was a series of questions that I had to answer before I could even do it. That’s not why I’m there. You shouldn’t have to put up with all that if you’re paying for an app that is supposed to bring you peace of mind.

reviews.title: Gamification detracts from contemplation
reviews.body: So when this app was commercialized, it did become really annoying. There are frequent requests for funds. I continue to use it because the one feature I use, the timer, can be engineered so that it opens immediately when you open the app. But at the end of each session, there is an obtrusive streak invitation that you have to either accept or swipe the app closed. And you actually have to get a paid membership to turn the streak pressure off. My meditation practice mostly takes place in the real world with my religious group, so repeated virtual streak invitations are a waste of time. And every time I finish a timer session, I lose a little bit of the peace of mind I gained to this app’s mindless attempts to gamify my mindfulness.

reviews.title: Was better before they over- thought it
reviews.body: This used to be a great app. They have added useless and time-consuming clicks, very mediocre daily quotes that I have to click through, continuous bait to subscribe to their “challenges“, that I find myself getting annoyed before and after every meditation that’s supposed to calm me down.  Many of their quotes are ridiculous and some are offensive - it would be better if they left them out rather than pretend to be profound, and in the process be irritating to  different belief systems.    And why after each meditation do I have to click five times in order to get out of the app and save my data. And no, I don’t care about my streak, that should be an opt out button.  I love the gongs and the bells and the timer. I don’t love no longer being able to find the meditations that I’ve enjoyed in the past, but being pushed into newer teachers, that I don’t particularly want to listen to.  I’m hoping a competitor will come along, so I will have another option for daily meditation timers.  Sorry to be negative when their mission is good but the developers need to rethink.

reviews.title: UI makes it impossible to find stuff
reviews.body: The constant UI changes are so frustrating! I love the meditations, but I cannot find anything I am looking for, which then makes what is supposed to promote relaxation stressful. I cannot find my bookmarks when they used to be easy to locate. Why so many changes that just bloat the app? It’s bad design.

great teachers and tracks, but the nagware interface is idiotic. If I'm trying to open it after five days because I'm having a panic attack or the like and need a talk-down, I do not have the capability to click through ten meaningless screens that can't be escaped.
I love the app but I absolutely hate the layout changes in the most recent update. Finding my bookmarks is no longer easy or intuitive.

reviews.title: What happened?
reviews.body: I’ve had this app since 2016, and never had this problem, but it’s been ongoing for months now snd hasn’t been fixed so now adjusting my review. Every time I open the app, it thinks it’s my first time logging in and had me go through the long I take questions every single time. Which has actually steered me away to not use this platform anymore. So developers, this is something to look into. Would love to come back!

Content is good but the amount of in-app popups and messages I have to tap through feels really intrusive and the transition animations are also slow. I turned off all notifications that I could but I still get welcome popups as well as messages after a meditation. I just want to pop in and pop out I don't care about my streak or being "commited". Please consider adding options to turn off these things and fix the slow transitions, it makes it very unpleasant to use as many others have said too.

app continues to run in the background even after I close it and force stop it. it will also start randomly playing through my phone or bluetooth device even after it was stopped/turned of hours prior.

reviews.title: Life changing
reviews.body: My ‘go to’ site for peace and acceptance for 14 years.

the forced check in if you've not visited in a while is abhorrent. I don't want to set goals and preferences and intentions if I am trying to manage uncomfortable feelings but there seems to be no way to opt out of this sequence on start up.

reviews.title: Was 5 stars
reviews.body: They got rid of the option to have your daily intention automatically repeat for a day, a week, a month. That’s gone now.

reviews.title: Destroying values
reviews.body: This app is a great tool, I just wish they would start living by the values they are trying to help people worth. Their goal is to help people live a better life yet they push push notifications even when I said no. It has happened twice. They make you go thought a survey when you come back, I don’t believe it is to be helpful, I see it as just another way for them to get more info on me.

Are you people crazy. Fire your product manager or whoever was stupid enough to force users into a 12 stage mandatory survey after returning to the app. I just wanted to meditate again, not populate your dam marketing data. Are you kidding me. I can't even skip questions. Seriously, what were you thinking jamming all that garbage between the user returning and getting value out of your app. What a joke.

reviews.title: Keeps getting worse
reviews.body:
More prompts to upgrade, and poor premium content.  The premium sounds are poor quality so I started to use brain.fm. Then the timer would be unreliable when I used 3rd party audio. Now they’ve added so many prompts to upgrade I’ve decide to uninstall and find something else entirely. 

I have 900 hours of meditation history on this app and it’s so bad now I’d rather lose it than keep being treated like a cash machine.

reviews.title: A bit annoying
reviews.body: Good app but these unskippable animations and commitments after meditating are annoying

reviews.title: Used to be far better
reviews.body: Originally downloaded this app about ten years ago and it was wonderful back then. I found about four meditations for anti-anxiety and sleep that I have gone back to repeatedly. However, two days ago I went back to this app after an unintended hiatus, and it pressured me to make an account, tried to coax me into paying for it, and WHAT REALLY DISAPPOINTS me is that I haven’t been able to find my top-favorite mountain themed sleep meditation. I wish I could at least remember the name of its male narrator. Anyway I tried sampling the mountain ones in a search this evening and none of them sound even remotely like the one I’m now missing. Unless I can find that one back, I might delete this app :(

reviews.title: Pretty good but with design flaws
reviews.body: I’ve used Insight Timer maybe 700 times so I’m definitely a “user.” It works fine but there is one big design flaw that is truly irritating. When you finish meditating, the “continue” (“finished” that is) button is right on top of a discard session button. Probably at least twice I week I finish meditating but discard the session if I’m not super careful to not brush the discard option. Why, oh why, are these two completely opposite and not recallable options stacked on top of one another! Plus, over the years, it seems like the app has become bloated with features. Some of us just want a meditation timer. The other features are great — but I wish there were just a minimalist timer setting so I don’t have to always skip past multiple things I’m not interested in. Just saying.

reviews.title: Meditation timer does not work
reviews.body: I really want to like this app and have been using it for months, but at this point, I have to stop because the core functionality, the meditation timer, simply does not work. it has a tendency to turn stop timing when the screen turns off. Which means that it's just unreliable. That's a pity, and I hope the team finds a way to sort this out, as it's been happening sporadically for the last 12 months.

too much premium content. I've been on insight timer for years. it used to be great. There used to be a lot of free content. But now they are heavily pushing their premium content. Teachers who used to publish a lot of free content now help us mostly premium stuff. Most of the free content doesn't seem interesting. The interesting stuff is locked behind a paywall.

The app is a great resource for meditative practices to suit all tastes and needs. But it is becoming increasingly cluttered with goal-oriented or competitive mindsets, forcing you to click through multiple "commitment" of goal setting screens (like Duolingo) at the end of each session. And like everything social media, gets used by MAM as a dating app. If you just want a zen experience, I recommend NOT using an attractive/feminine pic for profile.

There's a teacher on here called Shaun Ramsden from Australia. In his talk on this app 'How to Practise Buddhism (Lay People) he says people from Buddhist countries just pray and don't really practise Buddhism. Actually that is thought of as meditation and not prayer and if he bothered to do any sort of research he would hear the teachings in the chanting. He completely misses mentioning The 4 Brahmaviharas, the 5 hindrance, and loving kindness meditation, in addition to Sila.

reviews.title: So many questions
reviews.body: I used to love this app. The meditation tracks are great. I don’t use it every single morning and therefore every time I come back, they want me to spend a couple of minutes answering a bunch of questions rather than just being able to start using the app. I just want to use the timer and listen to the tracks, I don’t need to set goals or specify intentions or any of whatever other stuff they’re trying to track for their own marketing purposes. It’s a shame because the content is great, but it’s frustrating to try to use it.

reviews.title: Body scan
reviews.body: I'm so confused the description says that it's the worlds largest and best FREE APP, umm it was and then over a year ago-ish they charged me like $80 or more for a membership after having it for about 7-10 years when it was free. Or is it now a type to have two versions one that's garbage for free with ads and another overpriced full version? I'm annoyed (free amazing meditation would help me huge!) and confused. I'll delete this review it's a decent app still and has a GOOD free version of went all the way back to free, if not I'll keep the rating up. 2 stars for being good for years and -3 for not informing the people who had the app for a long period of time who then had to fight with Apple and insight to get their money back.

Total rip off. Charged me without my knowledge, only found out when I got my phone bill at the end of the month, then refused a refund. Not exactly reducing my stress, as they claim is their main aim. Their main aim is to make money. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Too many clicks to start a meditation now. They have a ridiculous number of screens and requests and offers and questions when you just want to engage with the actual soothing material. Then they want to ask you things after to pull you out of the mood. After is at least preferable. They make it a trail on the front end. July 2026 they made it even worse. Had to close the app and give up before even reaching a saved meditation. They're stressing people with questions polls and social nonsense

reviews.title: Stop the pop ups!
reviews.body:
I don’t want to be assaulted with the goal/moods pop ups when I open the app. 

It makes me use waking up instead.

I had to use this for therapy as my therapist needed to share content with me. I opted to stop the free trial, and was still charged for a yearly subscription. I believe this is a scam that is predatory towards those in need of help. I will not use this again.
Good variety of topics. Unfortunately the app forces you to have "Commitments" if you want to access the content.

Timer has become ever more unusable from what was once an oasis of calm & focus. I've used since 2015 but it's become too bloated, with distracting wellness & motivation prompts you can't turn off, in attempts to upsell. Have you never heard "less is more"?
I have really been enjoying this app but it's not working anymore! I open it and I can't get past the initial screen. The daily quote shows up then disappears and nothing happens!
pay to play

I really like this app but I feel really discriminated against to be honest. I am a late riser due to working 2pm to 11pm in my timezone. This means I am often going to bed well after midnight. I will often meditate 10am when I wake up, but sometimes I have a big morning and so will meditate before bed. Unfortunately Insight Time will register this as missing a day so it tells me I broke my streak. Please fix!

reviews.title: No timer
reviews.body: I don’t want all this stressy fuzz. Just the timer with the singing bowls. Like the years earlier. Nothing else.

reviews.title: FORCED activities you can’t skip!
reviews.body: If you go back to meditating after a long time away, it makes you answer 18,000 questions forces you to set goals and will not give you any opt out options to skip. I notified customer service about it. They did nothing. I went back k after time away, It did the same thing again. This is a new feature they have added. I had to go into my preferences and delete a bunch of stuff to make it force me to go straight to the timer, which is what I want. We’ll see if it works.

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.body: I was trying to watch a course which it wanted me to pay for. I checked out just to go back to the app to have the course completely disappear. No amount of searching would bring it up. If you’re going to buy a course, you should actually be able to watch it insight of being asking to go through an entire series of questions that are irrelevant to the course itself.

reviews.title: Predatory subscription
reviews.body: Haven’t used the app in ages. Didn’t realise the subscription had been renewed, no ability to request refund.

reviews.title: Pop ups are overstimulating
reviews.body: Insight has redesigned to have pop ups that force you to interact with the app to access and even finish/close meditations. This constant cycle is overstimulating, annoying, and obviously capitalistic. It’s hard to be in meditation when there are 15 things I have to click through to finish my meditation and go back to the home screen. Obviously - like insultingly so- designed to increase user engagement but completely diminishes the experience that the app is supposed to provide by employing gimicky tricks to lull users into engagement. Will be deleting.
it's become more annoying than before pushing "commitment"

Am I experiencing this glitch/bug because I am not a paying member? The app is great until you join the challenges. Sometimes it works.. but now with the new challenge, it keeps freezing and restarting the app. My mental health needs this.. but its not worth the trouble. The challenge is called: Somatics Challenge.

reviews.title: Was better before all the entry questions —gawd!!
reviews.body: Seriously…? Like way to get me all annoyed before trying to meditate. All these questions etc as to what my goal is and to make me commit… blah blah. I have ADHD and meditating is NOT going to happen for me every day. Like many things, it’s something that ebbs and flows in my life. Can that be ok?? Must you poke and prod me to meditate more than that??? So many apps are making apps more difficult to use to ‘increase engagement’ and be in the app longer than what the user really wants… I suppose you have investors to answer to? And all the while what is really happening (for me at least) is that tactics is steering me away from those tactics and LESS engagement. I DONT WANNA BE ADDICTED TO MY PHONE. Can that also be ok?? Starting to just feel like another metrics driven, greedy app

reviews.title: Way too easy to lose a streak
reviews.body: I was tapping to get into the actual app interface since it shows a quote in the splash screen, and it bypassed the ability to repair my streak and I lost my 200 day streak. So disappointing. Make it so that people have to tap an X to close the repair streak screen. I’m so upset that I spent 200 days building up this streak only for it to be lost because I tapped one too many times.

reviews.title: Nefarious UX
reviews.body: I use Insight Time to help me calm down and relax after stressful days. And, largely, the meditations do exactly that. But then after the meditation, the endless clicks, animations, and questions to get back out are infuriating, negating the effect of the session. Even worse, on a regular basis it replaces the “continue” button with an “install widget” button. Here’s a thought: if I wanted the widget I would have installed it by now. Why do you think trying to trick me into putting the widget onto my phone is a good idea? It makes me want to uninstall your app, not use it more.

my account keeps getting deactivated. I get logged out frequently. I'm supposed to sign up to join challenges and my password isn't recognised. I tried changing it and my account got disabled. terrible experience

reviews.title: Increasingly annoying changes
reviews.body:
The app has been changing a lot lately. It pushes a lot more Pro content, it tries to feed me videos and courses, and there is an uptick in AI. It’s frustrating that the section categories keep changing inexplicably. 
Wish it would let me set a bedtime to roll over the daily tracker. My job keeps me out late so I go to bed around midnight. If I’m even a few minutes late starting up the app, I lose my streak!

reviews.title: Get rid of required goals
reviews.body: Those goals are a pain to get past. I have the paid version and still have to choose goals before I can move on to my content.

reviews.title: Endless Ads
reviews.body: This used to be a great app. Now I have to go through 10 pages of „intention setting“ before I can even get to the timer. Ruins the entire experience.

reviews.title: Dead to me
reviews.body:
I’ll admit, I don’t use this app enough. So when I decided to get back on the bandwagon and reached for my “simple meditation timer” I was floored at what this app has become. 

This thing is a mess now. Just shilling and selling a subscription like every other app, to the detriment of the experience. It’s the OPPOSITE of calming. I JUST WANT A TIMER. 

I think at this point I’m going to just write my own app and give it away for free or a nominal charge and have something that’s actually useful.

reviews.title: Love the app… When I can actually get to it
reviews.body:
I swear to God if I have to go through another five minutes of stupid questions to open this app every time I’m going to throw my phone out the window. Which is kind of counterintuitive for this app.
Everything beside those questions is great

reviews.title: Just another money grabbing subscription app.
reviews.body: Don’t get stung by the ‘free trial’ strategy - you’ll end up with a yearly charge, randomly appear on your account ($89) and both the app and Apple blame each other and are practically impossible to contact to correct it.

App constantly crashes midway through a story. they make you pay for a subscription to fast forward anything so I'm stuck listening to the same first half of a story several times. It's also disruptive when I'm trying to sleep and the story stops midway through.

I've used this app for a decade and used to have the premium version. I loved it. It was the best meditation app available. It's now, sadly, undergoing the process of "enshitification" like so many other things in the virtual space 😥-- bloated with never-ending questions to complete that you cannot get around before getting to the main screen, deteriorated search function, etc. Very sad and frustrating.

I've been using this app for a while and have really been enjoying it. however, it has begun cutting out in the middle of meditations. it is beyond frustrating! I've tried all the recommended fixes and nothing works.

reviews.title: Recent problems with interface
reviews.body: I’m not sure what’s going on, but the meditation tracks are not loading smoothly or quickly. Also, the playlists won’t play. You start one track, and when it ends, the others won’t load. Please fix this, as I love this app!

reviews.title: Love the app, hate the update
reviews.body: This is a fantastic app in so many respects, and I use it for live yoga, timing self guided meditation, and guided meditation as well.  I’ve got a extensive library of guided meditations I’ve curated over the years, and with the latest update they are very difficult to access.  This creates a lot of unnecessary frustration.  This was a 5 star app before they messed around with it.  I hope that soon a new update will create a better fix than letting me pin one playlist to my home page.

I used to really love this app. It was my favorite go-to meditation app for years. Then slowly the enshittification began, more and more features being creeping in, the UI began changing, and pretty soon it was difficult to just use the timer. Now It's slow, full of ads, and bloated with extras. really leaves a bad taste in your mouth when the first thing you see before you meditate in the morning is an ad. Sad example of capitalism's creeping co-opting of everything real and good in the world

reviews.title: So disappointing
reviews.body: Insight Timer has changed for the worse. I regret that I didn’t cancel in time to avoid paying for it for a year. Some of the content is great. The app is very much not great.

reviews.title: Used to be good
reviews.body: This used to be the best app for meditation but they added a bunch of nonsense features that make it hard to use the actual bell which is the only feature I want. The bell still works alright once you mess with the settings so it’s not asking you to write a journal or share your practice with other people.

asked a million questions just to get to the sign up page, then couldn't sign in no matter what I tried just kept getting errors. automatically signs you up for an annual subscription even though you can't access content. I think this is a scam have cancelled and uninstalled. waste of time

This app regularly refreshes in the middle of a longer meditation, then does not allow you to pick up where you've left off unless you have premium. I tried all the fixes with no luck. I use this mostly for sleep meditations, so this issue made the app unusable for me.
Love it but why does it keep crashing just when I get nice and relaxed?!

reviews.title: Asks 1000 question before starting
reviews.body: Uninstalled without using, since it is asking to subscribe before  even giving some idea what is the app about.

reviews.title: 😢Future course bookmark list gone
reviews.body: I have calmly tried to go through the revamped app and found my profile with playlist. Don’t give a flying flip about my statistics. Had book marked future courses has disappeared. Can’t the app creators give us a warning when you’re about to do an update and disappear our stuff. Guess I’ll scroll through and search all the 7k courses to figure out what I vibe with.

reviews.title: Why make the animations longer?
reviews.body:
I’ve finished meditating, why extend the time it takes to convey all that ending info? Just because I’m in a relaxed state doesn’t mean I want to spend more time in the app

Also, stop asking me to add a widget

A meditation app adding annoyances is kinda hilarious

reviews.title: It has become too similar to social media apps
reviews.body: I’ve used this app for over 8 years, but in the last couple years, it’s become a spiral of endless prompts and requests to continue and do I want to commit to a streak. I have toggled off all the prompts that I can, yet I still need to press continue or skip several times just to wrap up a meditation and find the next one. I often listen to a guided meditation more than once or go from one to the next. What used to be a simple app focused on mindfulness (rather than profit) has become an app that utilizes persuasive design, a manipulative technique often used by prominent social media companies to create addiction-like behavior in users. I miss the focus on mindfulness, rather than dopamine. I am currently trying other apps. Update: Ooo Thich Nhat Hanh’s Plum Village app is sweet and focused on mindfulness, free, and surprisingly full of resources.

reviews.title: Can’t skip annoying pop ups
reviews.body:
I usually use this app when I can’t sleep, or when I am looking for a specific meditation. 

This app constantly wants me to set a goal, or set an intention. I understand that might be useful for some, but it’s not what I need. 

It’s very annoying to have to skip past three different screens that feel like they’re scolding me just to get to the sleep meditation I want. 

I paid for this app, but I will not be renewing my subscription when it runs out.

reviews.title: They make you sign up
reviews.body:
Cannot use the app without first personalizing the experience. User interface does not allow for continuing to use the app without answering "Tell me why you're here."  

Frustrating because I just want to use the app without having to give out this data to access the valuable content.

I want to be able to navigate the content without an AI personal assistant.
Happy New Islamic Year????
It takes >10 non optional screens to enter the app after installing on a new phone. This is not mindful. Or using again after a while. enshittified
Well, its free The search and filter does not always work (select male voice, no background music get results for with female voice with background music). there's also way too much content.

reviews.title: What happened?
reviews.body: As an off again, on again paid member, this app used to be great. There’s still great content, BUT I don’t want to constantly set goals, click thru pop ups, and I’m sick of getting the same 6 notifications at noon each day telling me to resume content I was interested in/completed in 2018 (despite having everything in encouragement and notifications turned off). Just stop!

This app is pathetic now. You have to take a quiz you can't exit out of about why you want to use the app or haven't used it in awhile after an absence of a few weeks. They start the timer with an unasked for chance at a free trial so I always have to manually go back to the presets in the timer. Every. Time. And then once the meditation is over there is another ad for the premium free trial. I am done with this app for good. It is some cliche money grab social media monstrosity.

Stops playing constantly! I downloaded this app and it looked pretty good, lots of options. One thing I didn't like was the talking in the beginning of many of the sleep audios. But the issue that made me delete the app was that on 3 of the 4 nights that I played a rainfall audio to help me sleep, it would stop playing out of nowhere. Only worked the first time I used it. So disappointing.

Like most, it sucks if you have aphantasia (the inability or low ability to visualize). and most of the time when I find a meditation that doesn't have the visualization tag, they've got long speeches with short meditations. If I want a speech I'll look for a talk. Searching for Aphantasia meditations suck too because they want to talk about it. That would be great if I didnt already have an understanding of it, but sometimes I'd like to have the same kind of meditations visualizers get to have!

why do I have to wait for an animation and press Continue and Finish about 6 times on different pages after I listen to something? it's the opposite of a well designed ux. Also the app tends to suggest paid content with higher ratings than the free content it shows in any suggestion list or search results, which suggests it isn't serving up the best free content.

The UI and functionality changes constantly! I mainly like this app for sounds to fall asleep to, and really like the sleep mixer feature. unfortunately, the sleep mixer seems to disappear from the app completely most days. not very relaxing when you just want to listen to the same thing every night. they also need to keep the buttons at the bottom the same. I like the content. need more long sleep tracks. sometimes the app shuts down before the playlist is done.

I just use this app for timing my meditation. It gradually gets worse for that with more pop ups and pointless screens. It's still better than finding a new app, but soon it will be time to switch, which is a shame.

I love the huge selection of meditations and music for every purpose; however, the app has changed over the years and become too complicated. There are so many icons on the homescreen that it is hard to find the few simple features that I actually want. After each meditation I have to click through so many different screens just to close it, which I find very annoying. After many years of membership with this app I've finally had enough of the frustrations and will now switch to something else.

reviews.title: done meditating? They want you to put money in the tip jar! after you pay for the app!
reviews.body: This was great when I first started using it, and I signed up for a year. At some point, they decided it was a good idea to ask for tips at the end of each experience. Like, “hey, our users are probably mellow right now. Let’s ask them for some money!”. It’s a total bummer and seems antithetical to the experience that people are trying to have. If I wanted to be pestered for money, I would sign up for our sicko president’s email list. WTAF? Did Elon Musk take over the app?

I used to love this app... but lately it is just getting bloated with pointless features that make it just harder and harder for me to use it. the most recent one is the daily streak animation, which takes forever. why do I need several button presses just to end something that is already finished? stop gamification please, it just makes it worse the only reason I keep using it is because I have my "history" here and would like to keep it.

I used to love this app when it was just guided meditations or a gong, but now the constant forced prompts and challenges to meditate daily are just really annoying and disruptive. I want a meditation app and have no need for the accountability but can't switch off

extremely annoying that when I go back into the app if I haven't used it in a while, I have to press so many buttons and can't skip the intake survey. I want to simply click on a meditation, or use the timer. all of the added fluff is simply added distraction.

I am really tired of the forced walk thrus of new features every time I login. I go to this app when I have 5 or 10 minutes to fit in a meditation in the course of a busy day. The forced engagement takes away from my time actually using the core features that I want to engage with, which are the meditation timer, and guided meditations. I hope they change this feature, because it’s unfair to the many incredibly talented practitioners who produce content for this app. But if they don’t change it soon, I’ll go elsewhere for my mindfulness content.

For example, when you install or reinstall the app, you must select a “streak” goal. I like being able to track progress, including consecutive days, but I really hate the judgy little peanut gallery that feels compelled to offer unwanted praise. 
I feel the consistency of my practice is nobody’s business but my own, and in fact I find it almost triggering to be judged about it. 
I’d cancel my subscription but I’ve been a member for 10 years, since before they started charging money for anything, and I guess I keep hoping they’ll make changes—for all I know there’s a way to turn off the judgement while keeping the tracking itself, but it’s certainly not in an obvious place.

reviews.title: Reviews correct BUT context needed
reviews.body:

The good news is you can avoid these unpleasant engagement strategies.

The bad news is you're still left with an app feeling disingenuous, with a misplaced philosophy of meditation and mindfulness. (Nudges are meant to be unintrusive, not pervasive) In other words: does this app actually drive good health outcomes, or just engagement?

I don't know if this is an inevitable consequence of the genre - or if it's the commercial pressure from being a venture based company (raised ~33M+ or thereabouts) 

In either case, it's a meditation app - some humility and sense of scope is important - on the part of users and the designers of these apps. I've been meditating for years and an app is very optional.
The timer itself is great, but the app has fallen into greedy, over the top incessant monetization.
I'm giving this rating because you guys have thousands of options for meditations, but no search bar. makes 0 sense.

was great. updates have slowly increased the number of intrusive clicks (commute to goals, etc) required to access the meditations. doesn't fit the vibe of a meditation app. still a great option, but it was better before

reviews.title: Too much information collected
reviews.body: I very much liked the app and the content was great. I was planning to purchase a subscription until I took a look at the amount of information that they collect. Too bad, it’s a good app.

Insight time is staring to feel like more of a car salesman than a relaxation app. The constant nagging and asking you do to better and make commitments to it makes it feel like a nagging parent instead of a helpful friend. It needs a setting to turn off all nagging. If i open up the app, I want to find what I am looking for, instead I constantly find myself trying to figure out the quickest way to dismissing the dialogs no one asked for.
It's difficult to find more secular oriented meditations

reviews.title: Why ruin it
reviews.body: Such a great app for ages now you have to constantly answer ad questions and other stuff. So disappointed as I loved this app for years

reviews.title: In-app prompts are a put off
reviews.body: I contacted the app developers late last year, no reply yet, about my experience of the prompts you can’t ignore, in that instance the ‘spotification’ / end of year data about how much I’d used the app. I explained why it’s a put off for me, it’s not neurodiversity friendly (PDA), and I’d searched long and hard in the app to find where to turn these notifications off so really didn’t appreciate multiple screens you have to go through (no opt out), thinking each was the last screen and not knowing how long this was going to go for, before you can use the app. After weeks of not using the app because of this very issue, I log on to see it’s happened again! This time, ‘welcome back’ followed by another 7 screens I can’t opt out of before I can even use the app. Between this and no reply to my contact, I am inclined to delete the app and cancel my subscription. Offering me a choice then ignoring my preference means this isn’t a safe place to go to when I need to calm my brain. I’d argue that neurodiverse people need meditation more than the average person, but we also need you to listen and grow when we give feedback. As it stands, I’ve paid for a service I now can’t use, and which doesn’t even acknowledge the gems in the feedback I provided.

The app is great, but the only issue is sync between devices. I have a dumb phone on which I have installed insight timer on, and I record almost all my meditation on it. But it often doesn't sync this data to the steak widget on my smartphone. Just recently, it reset my streak to 0 for a couple of days and I had to clear the storage on my main smartphone for it to get it back. But the main syncing issue is just that the streak widget doesn't update until the app is opened.

reviews.title: Pls let me meditate
reviews.body: Please stop setting goals and setting up other distractions on Insight Timer before allowing a user to access app. You don’t need to assume that I have not meditated or need anything other than access to features please.

I used to use Insight Timer daily (as a subscriber) because the actual content is great. However, it's become much more fiddly to access content, due to layout changes and too many prompts about goals/intentions etc, that I mainly use YouTube instead. It would really help to be able to customise the UI more, to limit distractions.

reviews.title: App’s user experience is just terrible…
reviews.body: The contents are fine, but the app itself is just so awkward and not functional enough. Please fix it from the ground up. reviews.body: I don’t know why they changed it every time you try to open it up all these things pop up and all you wanna do is get into meditation. It’s not relaxing whatsoever. Worst meditation app out there.

reviews.body: It requires an account now. For a while it's made you click through trite sayings before starting, then made you click through questions about how you're feeling after the meditation. Couldn't just keep a simple functionality as part of the app.

reviews.body: I have cancelled my subscription. It used to be a calming place that didn’t feel like an app. Now it feels like everything wrong with an app has been programmed into one place. reviews.body: Unskippable screen every time you open the app is the stupidest decision to gather 1* reviews.

reviews.body:
Attempted to capture clipboard contents on launch. Luckily, handoff prompts before allowing this when pasting from another machine. Clipboard contents should only be read when actually pressing the paste button as they can contain passwords or sensitive information.

Do not use this app.

reviews.title: Ads and popups
reviews.body: Too many ads for retreats or their premium service. Too many popups and prompts. It’s cluttered and messy.

Despite having all the notifications turned off on the app settings, I've been getting spammed for several days with notifications being me to use the app more. I'll use it when I want and how I want, these unwanted intrusions have me considering using a different app after 7 years.

reviews.body: I used to love Insight Timer and recommend it to everyone but there are so many questions and challenges now. I understand you need to grow and want paid. reviews.body: It doesn’t just let you use the timer without signing up for a free trial. No way to turn it off.

reviews.title: Excellent, except...
reviews.body: This comprehensive app has it all. I can see why my wellness coach recommended it. One feature, however, that I wish would change is the NOTIFICATIONS. While some users fully benefit from any level of notifications, including reminders and milestones, others, such as myself find notifications to be intrusive and interruptive. Although there is a feature to turn off specific types of notifications, even when every toggle is turned off and the app is closed on your phone, the app still prompts you, after a period of being away, through a unsolicited reminder notification to open the app. For occasional users such as me, this is quite annoying, and in no way prompts me to suddenly feel like meditating. Defeats the purpose, doesn't? Shouldn't the user decide when it's good timing to open the app? Not all users are motivated by milestones or levels of  engagement; yet when a user personalizes the notifications, the app is still programmed to disrespect the users's preferences. I like features like this with my exercise apps, but for meditation, the timing should come from the user. I'm going to offload the app for a while...

reviews.title: Increasingly over-engineered
reviews.body: Have been using this app for 5 or so years. It used to be a simple repository of meditations. Now it is over-complicated and increasingly filled with nonsense. Examples include constantly asking you how you are feeling, asking you to set intentions to meditate, and the barrage of questions you get once you finish a meditation. The sum of these is an interrupted experience that works directly contrary to  a central purpose (or at least former purpose, as now it has become as about as commercial as anything else) of the app: the relaxation associated with meditation.

reviews.title: Annoying survey
reviews.body: Love this app, have been using for years on the paid option. Please remove the recent addition of the compulsory survey - you enter the app ready to zen and get hot by a marketing survey - not cool! The app is 5 stars the survey is zero.

reviews.title: Great app but…
reviews.body:
Now has a million survey screens whenever I try to do anything. I don’t want to be asked a million questions every time, it’s crazy. Used to be better. I didn’t use it for a while and coming back I literally had to go through 10+ screens of questions. No skip options. I suggest you change this.

Hassle to log in, does not remember you

reviews.title: Timer can be improved hugely
reviews.body: I wanted to set specific time intervals for a meditation. I want to change to specific positions at specific times, hold the position for a time and have some time in the middle to set the next position. So I create a combination of 15’’, 3’, 20’’, 1.5’, etc. in that order. When I saved the timer it reorder all interval by the length of time: 15’’ first the 20’’ then 1.5’ and 3’ last and there is no way to set a specific order which is frustrating. I am sure this is not difficult to implement.

reviews.title: Forced upgrade begging prevented me from getting help during a panic attack.
reviews.body:
I was recently having a panic attack and reached for this app as a way of calming myself down. I was presented with an inescapable pattern of questions that leads nowhere but to an upgrade screen. A process I’ve had to endure many times over the past year or more. 

I’m my panicked state, I couldn’t even navigate the screens to get to a meditation. 

The commodification of wellness is disgusting and the monetization team should be ashamed of themselves for repeatedly standing in the way of people trying to seek help with the app’s free features!

reviews.title: Content is good but app is not great

reviews.body: I like having a timer to help me with my meditations, and IS used to great for this. Now it won’t let you get on with your meditation and insists you click through  endless nonsense before you can start your practice. Why are you here, what do you want, how long blah blah blah. reviews.body: I used to love this app honestly but every time I go to it I need to answer a million questions - I don’t want to think, I want to meditate. It shouldn’t be so mentally hard. So here we are. I get that sometimes those prompts may be nice but at least give us the option to exit out of it

reviews.body: The app used to be brilliant. However, every time I open it now I get bombarded with lots of questions. I just want to open the app and pick a meditation without answering a survey every time.

reviews.title: A shame really.
reviews.body: Have a look at how much of your data they gather before installing.

reviews.title: Disappointing Start
reviews.body: I wanted to use this to start my mornings well. I answered a great deal of questions to create my account eg like what my goals were reduce stress, mindfulness etc, then apparently a schedule would be set up for me. So in the morning I expected to go to the app to do the exercise set for that day. The next morning I checked the app and there was nothing set at all so I had to spend time looking through the various courses to see which one met my needs of 5 mins per day as I'd specified in the account creation questions. After 15 mins I decided I needed to get on with my day without this, but this has started my day with frustration rather than mindfulness! If you're not going to use my answers why waste my time with the useless questionnaire?!

reviews.title: Need to create an account ?
reviews.body: Was a daily user until today. Suddenly I’m forced to create an account. Ok….kind of spoils the mood but I created an account. Now my history is wiped. I’m now a newcomer. Consecutive days…gone. Saved tracks…gone.  Now I’m … gone.

reviews.title: Great content, awful app design
reviews.body: I love the meditations and content however, since they went back to the “2018” design I hate it. The world map is pointless. Go back to your previous update. Simpler, easier to see what courses you’ve started and continuing on. Easier to find the content and solve classes

reviews.title: Current layout isn’t helping my zen
reviews.body: While the meditation sessions are awesome, everything is so much harder to find now that you’ve changed it back to the 2018 version. I wish you would change it back. I find the layout confusing now; you are trying to be too many things for us: intentions, journal, quotes, gratitude, mood tracker, map, community… offer these if you like but organize it better. Personally, I’m just here to meditate. When I open the app it is usually to replay a meditation session I’m familiar with. But I’m forced to scroll past all these other bells and whistles features. It would be easier to make meditation a consistant habit if the sessions I’ve played before were easier to find. Make the sessions I’ve played often easier to find too. And have the sessions I haven’t tried yet in a separate Explore section. That way, if I’m in the mood for tried and true it’s easy to find, if I’m looking for a session I remember playing at some point and want to find it again, I know where to look, and if I’m in the mood for something new, I know where to click to find all of those. The meditation star streak badges are a good idea. I like knowing how often I’ve meditated and when. Keeping my streak alive would be more motivating if this feature was easier to find. I always kind of just chance on it. The other features mentioned earlier should all be in a separate tab as opposed to sitting in part of the feed of things I first see.

reviews.title: Functional but bloated
reviews.body: I found this app quite helpful but all I need is a meditation timer that logs minutes to the health app. That’s why I prefer the watch version so much more. When I try use the iOS app there’s far too much UI noise to click through. It’s commendable how many features I see, but annoying for someone who doesn’t need said features.

reviews.title: App has changed for the worst
reviews.body: Just want to log on to meditate not answer loads of questions and set goals NOW RUBBISH and not supporting proper meditation!

reviews.title: Dishonest
reviews.body: I honestly don’t know how I became a paid subscriber of this app as I did not know until I was six months in. When I queried it, customer service blamed Apple and took no responsibility for not being transparent with how it lures customers into purchasing a subscription without consent. Given they refused to refund me and Apple won’t because I was six months into the subscription, I tried to make use of the app but found it very disappointing.

reviews.title: They have hidden the timer!!

reviews.title: My spirituality isn’t an iPhone game.
reviews.body: This morning when I launched Insight Timer, the app noted that I hadn’t logged in yesterday. It prompted me to enter yesterday’s meditation, congratulated me for “protecting my streak,” and told me I had two more streak freezes this month. I was horrified, and I deleted the app immediately. Gamification is a dopamine harvesting strategy employed to keep people engaged with apps for the sake of money. Not only is it repulsive on its own, it has no place in a meditation app. Now that I know the company is only in it for the cash and is willing to sabotage my spiritual life for the sake of a payday, I urge all of you to delete Insight Timer immediately no matter what the company says in response to my review, if anything. Use a kitchen timer if you must, but don't give this abomination a red cent.

reviews.title: Now awful, avoid, avoid, avoid!
reviews.body:
Insight timer used to be really valuable even for the free version.
